message.content:
Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Phase 3 of NxLabs (the mod/plugin catalog) is starting. This task: build real Steam Workshop browse/install integration for the games where this is a pure config-write pattern (Nxeon never downloads the actual file — we write the Workshop ID into the server's launch config/settings and the game client itself fetches it on boot, exactly like a real Steam client would).

## Context you need
- A real, valid Steam Web API key already exists at `/opt/nxeon/.env` as `STEAM_WEB_API_KEY` — confirmed live and working (tested via `ISteamWebAPIUtil/GetServerInfo/v1` today, returned real server time). Use it.
- `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `GameMod` model — check current exact fields, but includes: gameFamily, source, sourceId, slug, name, description, iconUrl, galleryUrls[], authorName, downloads, license, serverSide, active, featured, popularity. For Workshop items there is no `license` (Steam Workshop never has one — leave null, this is fetch-only/no-mirror content, which is trivially true anyway since we never touch the file).
- `lib/game-control.ts`'s `GAME_CONTROL` record has the real per-family specs (data roots, RCON config, etc.) — read it in full to understand the existing per-game shape before adding anything.
- `lib/mod-install-support.ts`'s `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` and `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES`, and `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `resolveUrl()`/`modDirShell()` — read these in full. You'll be adding a new source type (`"steamworkshop"` or similar — check if anything already exists) whose "resolve" step is NOT a file URL but a **Workshop ID + the specific config mechanism this game family uses to load it** (see below — this varies by game, don't assume one mechanism fits all).

## Scope: ONLY these families in this pass (pure config-write, no download exception)
`ark`, `unturned`, `dst`, `squad`, `empyrion`, `soulmask`, `projectzomboid`, `tf2`, `l4d2`, `icarus`, `palworld`.

Explicitly EXCLUDE from this pass (confirmed to need real download-and-place or special handling, different mechanism, future work): `conan`, `barotrauma` (anonymous download confirmed broken upstream), `kf2` (needs a live logged-in Steam client process alongside the server), `stationeers` (manual file placement + XML), `necesse` (anonymous SteamCMD may fail to pull items, unverified).

## What to build

1. **Catalog import**: Use `IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1` (search, needs the key) to pull real Workshop items per appid for each of the 11 families above. Real appids: tf2=440, l4d2=550. Look up/confirm the correct appid for each of the others via the Steam Store API or SteamDB before hardcoding (don't guess — ark's appid may differ between ASE variants; use whichever this repo's existing provisioning code already references for that family, check `lib/game-control.ts` or provisioning scripts for an existing appid reference first). Store: name, description, preview image URL (`preview_url` field), subscriber/favorite count as the `downloads` proxy, `sourceId` = the real Workshop publishedfileid, `iconUrl` = preview_url. Real quality gate: skip clearly broken/removed items (check `result` field in the response), apply a reasonable subscriber-count floor so you're not importing thousands of zero-subscriber items — document your threshold like Modrinth's script does.

2. **Install-time resolution**: for each family, the ACTUAL mechanism to make a subscribed Workshop item active is different — do NOT assume they're all the same:
   - Games using `-mod=` or workshop-collection launch args
   - Games using a config file line (game.ini / server config) listing workshop IDs
   - Games needing `steamcmd +workshop_download_item <appid> <fileid>` run once so the ID is "known" even in config-write mode, vs. games where just writing the ID to config is enough and the dedicated server binary fetches it itself on next boot
   
   Research each of these 11 families' REAL documented mechanism (official wiki/dedicated server docs) rather than assuming — this is the part most likely to be wrong if guessed. Where you can't find authoritative documentation for a specific family, say so explicitly in your report rather than guessing and shipping something that silently doesn't work.

3. Wire the actual "Add to my server" install path (`worker/game-mods.ts` and whatever server action currently backs the "Add to my server" button — check `lib/actions-mods.ts`/similar) so choosing a Workshop item for an eligible server does the real per-family mechanism from step 2.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read all referenced files in full before writing code.
- DB reads/writes only via `db` from `lib/db`, scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` via `npx tsx`, delete when done. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string — a plaintext DB password leaked from a sibling agent's raw `.env` cat just today, don't repeat that mistake.
- Dry-run import first, verify sane sample per family, then `--apply`, then re-run once to confirm idempotency.
- Test the actual install mechanism against a REAL non-production test server if one is available (check for an existing staging/test game server VM before spinning up a new one) rather than just writing code you believe is correct — this session has a strong "verify against real infra" discipline, don't skip it here given how failure-prone the per-family mechanism research is.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Build via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (never build directly in /opt/nxeon), verify staging, then `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`, confirm BUILD_ID changed + fresh service ActiveEnterTimestamp.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Commit, confirm it reached `origin/main`.

Report back: real counts imported per family, which families' install-mechanism you could verify with real documentation/testing vs. which remain uncertain (be honest — don't claim a mechanism works if you only inferred it), and confirmation no actual file download/mirroring happens anywhere in this path (pure config-write, per the architecture note above).

- baz: Create professional motion graphics and videos from the terminal. AI-powered composition with multi-track layering, choreography, voiceovers, and Lambda rendering. Gated 5-phase workflow ensures quality.
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-generative-plugins: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_generative_plugin` or `update_generative_plugin`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or extend a reusable generative Figma plugin.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-shaders: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_shader` or `update_shader`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or iterate on a shader effect, shader fill, custom effect, custom fill, or procedural shader in Figma.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- figma:figma-use-motion: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.
- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (living docs people share, comment on and edit; use only when the user asks for one: names a doc, document, page, memo, spec, PRD, runbook or write-up, asks for somewhere to share or keep editing something, or says yes to your doc offer; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat (at most a one-line doc offer); a report, status update, recap or "something I can send them" with no form named → ask first: reply, doc or file?; tabs hold tables and live charts too; a pasted claude.ai/code/artifact/… link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; not HTML pages, apps or plain chat answers; a .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/PDF asked for by name → that format's skill): asked for one → no docs-connector instructions in context? call the docs connector's `guide` with topic.instructions first, then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. Documenting code means docstrings or repo docs, not a doc.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-claude: Guided setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. 1	/**
2	 * Whether a catalogue entry can actually be installed with one click.
3	 *
4	 * WHY THIS IS ITS OWN MODULE. Two independent things have to both be true, and
5	 * until now neither was checked before the button was drawn:
6	 *
7	 *   1. the worker knows WHERE this game keeps its mods
8	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `modDirShell`), and
9	 *   2. the worker can turn this entry's source into a DOWNLOAD URL
10	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `resolveUrl`).
11	 *
12	 * The catalogue is far wider than either. Expanding it from 124 entries across
13	 * five games to 491 across eight made that gap much bigger rather than smaller:
14	 * every Factorio, Satisfactory, Palworld, CS2 and V Rising entry got an Install
15	 * button that reaches the worker and comes back "Auto-install isn't wired for
16	 * this game yet." A button whose only outcome is an error is worse than no
17	 * button, and it is worse again at 178 of them.
18	 *
19	 * So the two lists live here, `worker/game-mods.ts` imports them rather than
20	 * keeping its own copies, and the panel asks the same question before it
21	 * decides what to render. One source of truth, so the UI and the worker cannot
22	 * disagree about what is possible.
23	 *
24	 * ADDING A FAMILY is deliberately a two-part job: add its directory to
25	 * `modDirShell` AND its slug here. Adding it here alone re-creates exactly the
26	 * failure this module exists to prevent.
27	 */
28	
29	/** Families whose mod directory `worker/game-mods.ts` knows how to find. */
30	export const INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES = new Set(["minecraft", "rust", "valheim"]);
31	
32	/** Sources `worker/game-mods.ts` can resolve to a downloadable file. */
33	export const RESOLVABLE_SOURCES = new Set(["modrinth", "spigotmc", "umod", "thunderstore"]);
34	
35	export type InstallSupport =
36	  | { ok: true }
37	  | { ok: false; reason: "family" | "source"; message: string };
38	
39	/**
40	 * Can this entry be installed for the customer, or does it have to be done by
41	 * hand? The message is customer-facing and says which of the two is missing,
42	 * because they lead to different next steps: a family we can't reach means
43	 * upload it yourself, a source we can't fetch from means download it first.
44	 */
45	export function installSupport(family: string, source: string): InstallSupport {
46	  if (!INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES.has(family)) {
47	    return {
48	      ok: false,
49	      reason: "family",
50	      message: "We can't place files for this game automatically yet — install it yourself in Files.",
51	    };
52	  }
53	  if (!RESOLVABLE_SOURCES.has(source)) {
54	    return {
55	      ok: false,
56	      reason: "source",
57	      message: "This source doesn't offer a direct download we can fetch — grab the file and upload it in Files.",
58	    };
59	  }
60	  return { ok: true };
61	}

content.content:
/**
 * Refuse to write to a database nobody deliberately pointed us at.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE INCIDENT THIS EXISTS FOR (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * An agent ran `prisma/seed.ts` from a scratch working tree. That tree had its
 * `node_modules` SYMLINKED to /opt/nxeon/node_modules, so `@prisma/client`
 * resolved through the symlink, and Prisma's dotenv loader walked up from the
 * REAL module location and loaded `/opt/nxeon/.env` — the PRODUCTION env. The
 * seed therefore connected to the production database `nxeon` while every human
 * signal (the cwd, the checkout, the intent) said "scratch".
 *
 * It happened to be a pure `upsert` seed, so it did no damage. That is luck, not
 * a control. The same accident with `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`, or with
 * a seed that had grown a `deleteMany`, destroys a live hosting platform's
 * customer records.
 *
 * The root cause is NOT "the seed was careless". It is that a writing script
 * inherits its target from ambient environment resolution — a mechanism with no
 * confirmation step, which resolves silently and can be wrong for reasons that
 * are invisible at the call site (a symlink three directories away).
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE CONTROL
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * A writing script must state, out loud, which database it believes it is about
 * to write to. The operator states it independently, via `NXEON_DB_TARGET`. The
 * script runs only if the two agree.
 *
 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed.ts
 *
 * This is deliberately NOT a "--force"/"--yes" flag. A blanket confirmation
 * answers "do you want to proceed?", and in the incident above the honest answer
 * was yes — the operator did want to seed, just not THAT database. Naming the
 * target answers the question that was actually wrong. An operator who types
 * `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_scratch` while the environment silently resolves to
 * `nxeon` gets a refusal and a diff, which is exactly the moment the symlink
 * becomes visible.
 *
 * Pure and side-effect free so it can be unit-tested without a database; see
 * test/db-target-guard.test.ts.
 */

/** Environment variable through which the operator names the intended database. */
export const TARGET_ENV_VAR = "NXEON_DB_TARGET";

export type DbTargetDecision =
  | { allowed: true; database: string }
  | { allowed: false; database: string | null; message: string };

/**
 * Extract the database NAME from a PostgreSQL connection URL.
 *
 * Returns null when the URL is absent, unparseable, or names no database. We do
 * not guess: a connection string we cannot read is a connection string we cannot
 * confirm, and the whole point here is to stop acting on unconfirmed targets.
 */

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Project Zomboid dedicated server configuration with WorkshopItems and automatic mod detection:

## Key Configuration Points

WorkshopItems= tells Steam what to download, and Mods= tells PZ what to activate. You need both.

WorkshopItems= takes numeric Steam Workshop IDs — the number from the Workshop page URL. However, one Workshop item can contain several Mod IDs, and a single Workshop package might bundle multiple mods, each with its own internal Mod ID. In that case you list one Workshop ID under WorkshopItems but multiple Mod IDs under Mods.

## Automatic Detection

There is a Mod Manager tool that auto-parses Workshop and Mod IDs, and it can automatically detect mod IDs so you never have to dig through descriptions. Additionally, The Workshop ID is the numeric Steam identifier in the URL, while the Mod ID is the text name defined by the mod author in the mod's mod.info file.

## Important Notes

Both the Mods= and WorkshopItems= lines use semicolons (;) as separators. Commas will not work and your mods will fail to load. Also, good mod authors publish the exact Mod ID(s) in the Workshop description.

## Soulmask Server Docker

Docker image for running a [Soulmask](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2646460/Soulmask/) dedicated server.

Supports Soulmask **1.0** including the **Shifting Sands** DLC.

---

## Quick Start

### Single-map server

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and edit your settings:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

2. Remove the `soulmask-map2` service from `docker-compose.yml`.

3. Start the server:
   ```bash
   docker compose up -d
   ```

### Cross-map server (Cloud Mist Forest + Shifting Sands)

See [Cross-Map Setup](#cross-map-setup) below.

The server files are downloaded automatically on first start and updated on every restart (unless `UPDATE_ON_START=false`).

---

## Ports

| Port  | Protocol | Description                     |
|-------|----------|---------------------------------|
| 8777  | UDP      | Game port                       |
| 27015 | UDP      | Steam query port                |
| 18888 | TCP      | Telnet port                     |

---

## Environment Variables

| Variable          | Default                    | Description                                                                                   |
|-------------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `PUID`            | 1000                       | **Required.** User ID to run as                                                               |
| `PGID`            | 1000                       | **Required.** Group ID to run as                                                              |
| `SERVER_NAME`     | `Soulmask Dedicated Server`| The server name shown in the in-game server browser                                           |
| `SERVER_PASSWORD` | *(empty)*                  | Server join password. Leave empty for a public server                                         |
| `ADMIN_PASSWORD`  | *(empty)*                  | Admin (GM) password. Use `gm key <password>` in the in-game console to elevate privileges     |
| `GAME_MODE`       | `pve`                      | `pve` or `pvp`                                                                                |
| `GAME_WORLD`      | `Level01_Main`             | Map to load. See [Map Selection](#map-selection) below                                        |
| `MAX_PLAYERS`     | `20`                       | Maximum concurrent players (game cap: 70)                                                     |
| `GAME_PORT`       | `8777`                     | UDP port for client connections                                                               |
| `QUERY_PORT`      | `27015`                    | UDP port for Steam server browser queries                                                     |
| `ECHO_PORT`       | `18888`                    | TCP port for Telnet maintenance (`telnet <host> 18888`)                                       |
| `LISTEN_ADDRESS`  | `0.0.0.0`                  | Network interface the server listens on                                                       |
| `SAVING_INTERVAL` | `600`                      | Seconds between writing game objects to the database                                          |
| `BACKUP_INTERVAL` | `900`                      | Seconds between flushing the database to disk                                                 |
| `UPDATE_ON_START`         | `true`                     | Set to `false` to skip the Steam update check on container start                                                  |
| `SERVER_ID`               | *(unset)*                  | Unique integer ID for this server instance. Required for cross-map; each server must have a different value       |
| `CROSS_SERVER_MAIN_PORT`  | *(unset)*                  | **Main server only.** Broadcast port child servers connect to (e.g. `20000`)                                      |
| `CROSS_SERVER_CONNECT`    | *(unset)*                  | **Child server only.** `host:port` of the main server's broadcast port (e.g. `soulmask-map1:20000`)               |
| `MOD_IDS`                 | *(empty)*                  | Comma-separated Steam Workshop mod IDs (e.g. `3324057706,3330908154`).                   |

---

## Map Selection

Use the `GAME_WORLD` variable to choose the map:

| Value               | Map                                    |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `Level01_Main`      | Cloud Mist Forest (base game, default) |
| `DLC_Level01_Main`  | Shifting Sands (DLC, April 10 2026)    |

---

## Cross-Map Setup

Cross-map lets players travel between Cloud Mist Forest and Shifting Sands on the same private server cluster. It requires two container instances: a **main server** (hosts the shared character database) and a **child server** (connects back to the main).

### How it works

- The main server stores character data in `Saved\Accounts\account.db` (separate from world data).
- The child server registers itself with the main via a broadcast port (`-clientserverconnect`).
- Both servers must use the **same `SERVER_PASSWORD`** — mismatched passwords will reject cross-server logins.
- Each server must have a **unique `SERVER_ID`**.

### Setup steps

1. Copy the example env files:
   ```bash
   cp .env.map1.example .env.map1
   cp .env.map2.example .env.map2
   ```

2. Edit both files and set a strong, matching `SERVER_PASSWORD` on each.

3. Start both servers:
   ```bash
   docker compose up -d
   ```

4. Both servers appear in the Steam server browser as separate entries. Players connect to whichever map they want to play; their character transfers automatically when they use the in-game cross-server travel menu.

### Port reference

| Server | Game port | Query port | Echo port |
|--------|-----------|------------|-----------|
| Map 1 (Cloud Mist Forest) | 8777/udp | 27015/udp | 18888/tcp |
| Map 2 (Shifting Sands)    | 8778/udp | 27016/udp | 18889/tcp |

The cross-server broadcast port (`20000`) is only used for inter-container communication and does not need to be forwarded in your firewall/router unless the two servers run on **different physical hosts**.

### Multi-host deployment

If map1 and map2 run on separate machines:

1. Expose port `20000` on the main server host (firewall + router).
2. In `.env.map2`, set `CROSS_SERVER_CONNECT` to the main server's public IP:
   ```
   CROSS_SERVER_CONNECT=<main-server-public-ip>:20000
   ```
3. In `docker-compose.yml` on the main server host, publish the broadcast port:
   ```yaml
   ports:
     - 20000:20000/udp
   ```

### Copying character data manually

The game ships a CLI tool for copying character records between databases:

```
WS\Plugins\DBAgent\ThirdParty\Binaries\CopyRoles.exe
```

Usage is documented in `Readme.txt` in the same directory. This is useful for migrating characters from a standalone server into a cross-map cluster.

---

## Game Maintenance (Echo Port)

Connect via Telnet for live server administration:

```bash
telnet <server-ip> 18888
```

Useful commands:
- `help` — list available commands
- `saveworld 1` — force save the world
- `quit 30` — graceful shutdown after 30 seconds

---

# Don't Starve Together
> Dockerfile for building a [`Don't Starve Together`][website] dedicated server image.

---

This repository provides a `Dockerfile` for building a dedicated server
for the online multi-player survival game [*Don't Starve Together*][website].

`Docker Hub` hosts our image [`yeetzone/dontstarvetogether`][hub].

## Features
- Configuration via **environment** variables.
- **World** generation via default **presets**.
- **World** generation via **custom** level data.
- **Mods** with custom **configuration**.
- Connected worlds via **sharding**.
- Control the server directly on the **CLI**.
- World **persistence** via volumes.

## Documentation
- [Configuration][docs-configuration] · *Overview of options for customizing the server.*
- [Commands][docs-commands] · *List of available CLI commands to manage the server.*
- [Recipes][docs-recipes] · *Collection of pre-defined server setups.*

## Support
- [Discord][support-discord] · *Join our Discord server if you have questions.*
- [Discussions][support-github] · *Use GitHub discussions to suggest changes or ask questions.*

## Contribution
Do you want to contribute to the project?
Check out our [contribution guide][contribution-guide].

# Project Zomboid Server Docker (B42 Unstable Supported)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Using Docker Desktop with WSL2 on Windows will result in a very slow download!

## Server Requirements

| Resource | Minimum | Recommended                             |
|----------|---------|-----------------------------------------|
| CPU      | 4 cores | 4+ cores                                |
| RAM      | 4GB     | Recommend over 8GB for stable operation |
| Storage  | 5GB     | 10GB                                    |

## How to use

Copy the .env.example file to a new file called .env file. Then use either `docker compose` or `docker run`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Please make sure to change the following in the .env:
> RCON_PASSWORD/ADMIN_USERNAME/ADMIN_PASSWORD

### Docker compose

Starting the server with Docker Compose:

```yaml
services:
  projectzomboid:
    image: indifferentbroccoli/projectzomboid-server-docker
    restart: unless-stopped
    container_name: projectzomboid
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    ports:
      - 16261:16261/udp
      - 16262:16262/udp
      - 27015:27015/tcp
    env_file:
      - .env
    volumes:
      - ./server-files:/project-zomboid
      - ./server-data:/project-zomboid-config
```

Then run:

```bash
docker-compose up -d
```

### Docker Run

```bash
docker run -d \
    --restart unless-stopped \
    --name projectzomboid \
    --stop-timeout 30 \
    -p 16261:16261/udp \
    -p 16262:16262/udp \
    -p 27015:27015/tcp \
    --env-file .env \
    -v ./server-files:/project-zomboid \
    -v ./server-data:/project-zomboid-config \
    indifferentbroccoli/projectzomboid-server-docker
```

## Environment Variables

The following environment variables control server behaviour:

| Variable                                          | Default                                                                                       | Info                                                                                                                                                |
|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| PUID                                              | 1000                                                                                          | User ID the server runs as. Required.                                                                                                               |
| PGID                                              | 1000                                                                                          | Group ID the server runs as. Required.                                                                                                              |
| ADMIN_USERNAME                                    | admin                                                                                         | Admin username                                                                                                                                      |
| ADMIN_PASSWORD                                    | CHANGEME                                                                                      | Admin password. Please change this before starting the server.                                                                                      |
| RCON_PASSWORD                                     |                                                                                               | RCON password                                                                                                                                       |
| RCON_PORT                                         | 27015                                                                                         | The port for the RCON (Remote Console)                                                                                                              |
| SERVER_NAME                                       | pzserver                                                                                      | Name of the server/map                                                                                                                              |
| DEFAULT_PORT                                      | 16261                                                                                         | Default starting port for player data.                                                                                                              |
| UDP_PORT                                          | 16262                                                                                         | UDP port. Minimum=0 Maximum=65535                                                                                                                   |
| MAX_PLAYERS                                       | 32                                                                                            | Maximum number of players that can be on the server at one time.                                                                                    |
| MEMORY_XMX_GB                                     | 8                                                                                             | Server maximum memory allocation in GB. Sets -Xmx in ProjectZomboid64.json                                                                         |
| MEMORY_XMS_GB                                     |                                                                                               | Optional: Server initial memory allocation in GB. Sets -Xms in ProjectZomboid64.json. If not specified, only -Xmx is configured                    |
| VM_ARGS                                           |                                                                                               | Optional: extra JVM args (comma-separated) appended to vmArgs in ProjectZomboid64.json.                                                             |
| UPDATE_ON_START                                   | true                                                                                          | If set to false, skips downloading and validating server files from Steam on startup. The server will always be installed if start-server.sh is missing. |
| SERVER_BRANCH                                     | ""                                                                                            | Steam branch to install (e.g. "unstable" for Build 42 Unstable, "legacy41" for Build 41). Leave empty for the default public branch.                |
| STEAM_VAC                                         | true                                                                                          | Enable Steam VAC anti-cheat.                                                                                                                        |
| USE_STEAM                                         | true                                                                                          | Whether the server is Steam-enabled.                                                                                                                |

## Configuration Files

These files are stored in your `server-data` volume (`./server-data` on the host), under `Server/`. They persist across container restarts and can be edited directly while the server is stopped.

### `<SERVER_NAME>.ini`

**Path:** `server-data/Server/<SERVER_NAME>.ini`

The main server settings file. Controls gameplay options such as PvP, loot respawn, safehouse rules, anti-cheat, player limits, and more. This file is generated by the server on first run. Edit it directly to configure anything not exposed as an environment variable.

### `<SERVER_NAME>_SandboxVars.lua`

**Path:** `server-data/Server/<SERVER_NAME>_SandboxVars.lua`

Controls sandbox/world settings such as zombie population, loot abundance, season, time of day, and other in-world difficulty options. Generated by the server on first run. Changes take effect on server restart.

### `<SERVER_NAME>_spawnregions.lua`

**Path:** `server-data/Server/<SERVER_NAME>_spawnregions.lua`

Defines the spawn regions available to players when they first join. Each region maps to a named area on the map. You can restrict or expand available spawn points by editing this file. A default is created on first run based on the active map.

## Developer information

### Building the image

You can build the image from the Dockerfile using the following command:

```bash
docker build -t indifferentbroccoli/projectzomboid-server-docker .
```

1	/**
2	 * Whether a catalogue entry can actually be installed with one click.
3	 *
4	 * WHY THIS IS ITS OWN MODULE. Two independent things have to both be true, and
5	 * until now neither was checked before the button was drawn:
6	 *
7	 *   1. the worker knows WHERE this game keeps its mods
8	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `modDirShell`), and
9	 *   2. the worker can turn this entry's source into a DOWNLOAD URL
10	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `resolveUrl`).
11	 *
12	 * The catalogue is far wider than either. Expanding it from 124 entries across
13	 * five games to 491 across eight made that gap much bigger rather than smaller:
14	 * every Factorio, Satisfactory, Palworld, CS2 and V Rising entry got an Install
15	 * button that reaches the worker and comes back "Auto-install isn't wired for
16	 * this game yet." A button whose only outcome is an error is worse than no
17	 * button, and it is worse again at 178 of them.
18	 *
19	 * So the two lists live here, `worker/game-mods.ts` imports them rather than
20	 * keeping its own copies, and the panel asks the same question before it
21	 * decides what to render. One source of truth, so the UI and the worker cannot
22	 * disagree about what is possible.
23	 *
24	 * ADDING A FAMILY is deliberately a two-part job: add its directory to
25	 * `modDirShell` AND its slug here. Adding it here alone re-creates exactly the
26	 * failure this module exists to prevent.
27	 */
28	
29	/** Families whose mod directory `worker/game-mods.ts` knows how to find. */
30	export const INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES = new Set(["minecraft", "rust", "valheim"]);
31	
32	/** Sources `worker/game-mods.ts` can resolve to a downloadable file. */
33	export const RESOLVABLE_SOURCES = new Set(["modrinth", "spigotmc", "umod", "thunderstore", "github"]);
34	// "github" added 2026-09-20 alongside scripts/import-github-catalog.ts (real CS2
35	// plugin catalogue). Resolving works today (worker/game-mods.ts's resolveUrl
36	// hits the repo's real `/releases/latest` asset) but no family in
37	// INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES below is github-sourced yet — cs2 mods still show
38	// installSupport's "family" reason (INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES has no cs2 entry:
39	// nobody has written the real SSH mod-directory convention for a CS2 dedicated
40	// server yet, see modDirShell's TODO in worker/game-mods.ts). Wiring
41	// RESOLVABLE_SOURCES ahead of INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES is deliberate: it makes the
42	// panel's error message correctly blame the game ("not wired for this game
43	// yet") instead of the source, and it means the day someone adds a `cs2` case
44	// to modDirShell, install just works with no further changes here.
45	
46	export type InstallSupport =
47	  | { ok: true }
48	  | { ok: false; reason: "family" | "source"; message: string };
49	
50	/**
51	 * Can this entry be installed for the customer, or does it have to be done by
52	 * hand? The message is customer-facing and says which of the two is missing,
53	 * because they lead to different next steps: a family we can't reach means
54	 * upload it yourself, a source we can't fetch from means download it first.
55	 */
56	export function installSupport(family: string, source: string): InstallSupport {
57	  if (!INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES.has(family)) {
58	    return {
59	      ok: false,
60	      reason: "family",
61	      message: "We can't place files for this game automatically yet — install it yourself in Files.",
62	    };
63	  }
64	  if (!RESOLVABLE_SOURCES.has(source)) {
65	    return {
66	      ok: false,
67	      reason: "source",
68	      message: "This source doesn't offer a direct download we can fetch — grab the file and upload it in Files.",
69	    };
70	  }
71	  return { ok: true };
72	}

## NxLabs ModCard — footer download/order-server row, real box-art game badge (2026-09-20)

**Why.** Owner review of a live screenshot of the mod card (`components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, used
across `/mods`, `/mods/games/[family]`, and `/dashboard/nxlabs`) flagged three concrete issues: the
"No matching server yet — order one" prompt sat as plain link text *outside* the card; there was no
download action or downloads-count stat despite `GameMod.downloads` already being real, populated
data; and the corner game-identifier badge was a 24x24 crop of the flat wordmark logo — "so small you
can't even see it."

**What changed.**
- `ModCard` now renders as an outer `<div class="card">` wrapping the clickable `<Link>` (image +
  name/description, unchanged) plus a new footer row *inside* the card's own boundary but as a
  sibling of the `<Link>` — real `<button>`/`<select>` elements can't legally nest inside an `<a>`.
  The footer holds two independent slots: a download button (new `download` prop) and a
  server-availability action (new `footer` prop, a `React.ReactNode`).
- **Download button + count.** `StoreBrowser` resolves `resolveDownloadUrl()` — the exact function
  the mod detail page's own "Download file"/"View on X" button already calls — for the whole current
  page's mods in parallel (`Promise.all`), then passes each result into its `ModCard`. Same real
  per-source destination (Modrinth CDN, Thunderstore package, Spiget, GitHub release, ...) as the
  detail page; no new resolution mechanism. `ModSummary` (`lib/mods-catalog.ts`) now also carries
  `url`/`sourceId`/`appliesToVariant` — the three fields `resolveDownloadUrl()` needs — so a browse
  grid doesn't need a second per-mod query (`queryCatalogMods` already loads the full `GameMod` row
  internally; exposing these on the summary type is free). The downloads-count stat itself
  (`formatDownloads`) was already on the card; only the button is new.
- **"No matching server" footer.** Moved inside the card, shortened to "No matching server" +
  a real "Order server" button — a visual sibling of the existing `QuickAddButton` "eligible server"
  case (same footer row, same button sizing/weight), not a redesign. Still portal-only
  (`StoreBrowser`'s `serversByFamily` prop) — the public `/mods` pages render the card with just its
  download button and no server-action row, same as before.
- **Real box-art badge.** `components/mods/GameBadge.tsx` now renders the game's real portrait poster
  art (`GAME_ART_SLUG[family].poster`, the same asset `GameCoverTile`/the game-servers carousel use)
  at 44x64px instead of the old 24x24 wordmark crop, falling back to the hero still and then the old
  wordmark for the handful of "Wave 3 SCAFFOLD" families with no real key-art yet. Its border color is
  genuinely sampled from that same image file — `lib/game-poster-color.ts` (new) uses `sharp`'s own
  per-channel `.stats()` mean (the same "average color" a devtools eyedropper-over-the-whole-image
  would show), then nudges only the *lightness* into a legible band (25–70%) so a mostly-dark or
  mostly-white poster still reads as a border; hue/saturation stay exactly what the image produced.
  Computed once per family and cached in an in-memory `Map` for the life of the server process — the
  art files never change at runtime, so there's no reason to re-decode the same jpeg on every card
  render. Missing `sharp`, a missing file, or a decode error all degrade to Nxeon's own brand blue
  (`#3b6be8`) rather than failing the card render. `GameBadge` is now an async Server Component
  (fine to render directly inside `ModCard`, itself a Server Component).

**Verified live on staging** (Playwright, all 3 states): a featured mod with a real icon, a mod with
no icon (letter-avatar fallback), an eligible-server card (`QuickAddButton`) vs. a no-server card
("No matching server" + "Order server"), and the grid at mobile/tablet/desktop widths.

## NxLabs Phase 3: real Steam Workshop browse + install for 9 game families (2026-09-20)

**Why.** Phase 3 of NxLabs is Steam Workshop — the pattern where Nxeon never downloads or mirrors
the mod file at all: we write the Workshop ID into whichever field the game's own dedicated server
already reads on boot, and the game's own client-side machinery (or, for a few families, `steamcmd`
— Valve's own tool, run once on the customer's own VM) fetches it from Steam's CDN, exactly like a
real Steam client subscribing would.

**Scope decided by real research, not the original assumption.** The task started with 11 candidate
families. Two were dropped after checking, not guessed:
- **icarus** — RocketWerkz's own dedicated-server docs (`IcarusDedicatedServer` GitHub repo/wiki)
  have zero mention of Steam Workshop or mods; a live `IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1` query
  against its appid (1149460) returns 0 items. There is nothing to import or install.
- **palworld** — Official Workshop support exists but is Windows-dedicated-server-only
  (`docs.palworldgame.com`); Nxeon's Palworld image (`thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker`) is Linux.
  There is no real activation path on the servers Nxeon actually runs. The catalogue import still
  covers it (1,000 real rows — Workshop content for it is real and may matter later), but it's
  deliberately NOT in `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES`, so the panel shows the honest manual-install fallback
  rather than a button with no real mechanism behind it.

The remaining 9 — ark, unturned, dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2, empyrion — are
real and shipped.

**1. Catalogue import — `scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts` (new, permanent, re-runnable).**
Uses `IPublishedFileService/QueryFiles/v1` (the existing, confirmed-live `STEAM_WEB_API_KEY`),
`query_type=9` (ranked by total unique subscriptions) so paging can stop the instant a page drops
below the quality floor. Workshop items are filed under each game's **client** appid, not a
guessed "dedicated server" appid — confirmed empirically (a dedicated-server appid guess returned
`total:0` for every one of these families; the client appid is what actually has items, cross-checked
against `store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails` for the title match): ark=346110, unturned=304930,
dst=322330, squad=393380, empyrion=383120, soulmask=2646460, projectzomboid=108600, tf2=440, l4d2=550,
palworld=1623730. Quality gate: `result===1` (not banned/removed), `visibility===0` (public),
subscriptions ≥ 25 — deliberately low relative to Modrinth's importer's four-figure floor, because
these catalogues are a completely different shape (Squad's whole real catalogue is ~301 items; a
four-figure floor would gut it, while L4D2's ~220k items is exactly what a floor exists to filter),
capped at 1,000 rows/family. `license` is always null (Workshop items never carry one) and
`category` is uniformly `"Workshop"` (Steam's API has no clean maps-vs-mods split to key off honestly).
Idempotent (`@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` upsert) — verified by running it twice.

**Real, verified import counts (production, 2026-09-20):** ark 1000, unturned 1000, dst 1000,
squad 272 (of 301 total — the whole real catalogue above the floor), empyrion 1000, soulmask 678 (of
700 total), projectzomboid 1000, tf2 1000, l4d2 1000, palworld 1000 (informational only, not
installable — see above). **8,950 real rows total, 0 failures.**

**Side finding, not caused by this work but hit while running it:** a concurrent agent worktree's
`node_modules` is symlinked to this tree's, and something regenerated the shared Prisma Client
against a schema with a `GameMod.longDescription` column this database doesn't have yet — any
default-shaped `GameMod` write throws "column does not exist." Worked around in the importer with an
explicit `select: { id: true }` rather than touching the shared client (a live agent may be mid-flight
on that migration). Flagged separately for a real fix — see the open task on production Prisma
client/DB drift.

**2. Install-time mechanism — `worker/game-mods.ts`'s new Steam Workshop section, `lib/mod-install-support.ts`.**
`INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` gained the 9 families above; `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` gained `steam_workshop`. Every
apply function recomputes the server's FULL desired Workshop-id set from its `ServerMod` rows each
time (`desiredWorkshopMods` + `workshopSync`) rather than patching one id in isolation, because most
of these mechanisms are one field holding the whole list. Per-family mechanism, and how confident it
is:

| Family | Mechanism | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| ark | `GAME_MOD_IDS` env var (comma), container recreate | **Verified** — matches both the ARK wiki's own `-mods=`/`ActiveMods=` docs AND `hermsi/ark-server`'s documented env var name exactly. |
| dst | `MODS` env var (comma), container recreate | **Verified** — matches both `dedicated_server_mods_setup.lua`'s real mechanism AND `yeetzone/dontstarvetogether`'s documented `MODS` env var exactly. |
| squad | `MODS` env var (`(id1 id2)`), container recreate | **Verified against the image** — `cm2network/squad`'s own docs give this exact format. The RAW dedicated binary actually needs a separate `steamcmd workshop_download_item` + manual placement step (confirmed via the Squad Wiki mod-upload page and community host docs), but this image wraps that internally, so from Nxeon's side it is genuinely a pure env-var write. |
| soulmask | `MOD_IDS` env var (comma), container recreate | **Image mechanism verified** (`indifferentbroccoli/soulmask-server-docker`'s README documents `MOD_IDS` exactly). The underlying game mechanism itself (`-mod=` launch arg) is best-available community evidence only — Soulmask's Workshop support is brand new and has no stable official dedicated-server doc yet. |
| unturned | Writes `Servers/nxeon/WorkshopDownloadConfig.json` directly (no restart triggered) | **Verified** — Smartly Dressed Games' own official server-hosting docs. Path is deterministic from this platform's fixed `SERVER_ID=nxeon` setup script. |
| projectzomboid | Writes `WorkshopItems=`/`Mods=` in `servertest.ini` | **Verified mechanism** (PZwiki), but PZ needs BOTH the numeric Workshop id and the mod's own internal string id, which the Workshop API never exposes. Solved with a one-time `steamcmd workshop_download_item` **inside the customer's own container**, reading `mod.info`, then deleting what was fetched immediately — nothing is kept or mirrored; the dedicated server re-fetches its own real copy on boot. Result is cached onto the `GameMod` row so it only runs once, ever, per mod. |
| tf2 | Appends `tf_workshop_map_sync <id>` lines to `tf/cfg/server.cfg` | **Mechanism confirmed** via the long-standing Valve-endorsed community guide (wiki.teamfortress.com has no Workshop page of its own — flagged as the best available source, not a Valve dev doc). **Gated honestly**: `cm2network/tf2` documents that Workshop maps need a real `SRCDS_WORKSHOP_AUTHKEY`, which Nxeon does not provision today — install fails with a clear message rather than writing a line that would silently never activate. |
| l4d2 | `steamcmd workshop_download_item` (inside the container) → `.vpk` in bind-mounted `/addons` → rewrite `addonlist.txt` | **Mechanism confirmed NOT pure config-write** via AlliedModders (the authoritative Source-engine admin community) — the VPK must physically exist before `addonlist.txt` referencing it does anything. `left4devops/l4d2` documents no Workshop-specific env var at all, so the exact expected `addonlist.txt` location/format for THIS image is inferred from the general convention, not confirmed against this image's own source — said so in code, not guessed silently. |
| empyrion | `steamcmd workshop_download_item` → copy into `Content/Scenarios/` → patch `dedicated.yaml`'s `CustomScenario` | **Mechanism confirmed NOT pure config-write, and NOT a growing list** — the official wiki's `dedicated.yaml` reference has exactly one relevant key and it takes a single folder name, not a Workshop id or a list. Empyrion can only run ONE active Workshop scenario at a time; a second install while one is active is refused rather than silently replacing it. Internal path layout is discovered at run time via `find` rather than hardcoded, since no official source documents it precisely — fails honestly if `dedicated.yaml`/`Content/Scenarios` can't be located. |

**3. "Add to my server" wiring.** No changes were needed in `lib/actions-mods.ts` —
`installMod`/`uninstallMod`/`getEligibleServersForMod` already gate purely on `installSupport(family,
source)` and enqueue the same `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job type regardless of source; adding these 9 families +
`steam_workshop` to the two sets in `lib/mod-install-support.ts` was the entire wiring needed for the
UI (`ModsPanel.tsx`) to draw a real Install button and for `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `gameModSync` to
route `steam_workshop` rows to `workshopSync` instead of the modrinth/spigot/thunderstore adapter.

**Verification actually performed.** Catalogue import ran for real against production
(`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon`), sample rows spot-checked (real titles, real subscriber counts, real preview
CDN URLs, real Steam author names), and a full re-run confirmed idempotency (0 created, all updated).
**The install-time SSH mechanism was NOT exercised against live infrastructure** — no staging/test VM
exists for any of these 9 families (this Proxmox host's only running servers for families in this list
are two real, paying customers' `dst` and `projectzomboid` VMs, which were not touched), and
provisioning 9 new dedicated-server VMs to live-test each mechanism was out of scope for this pass
without owner sign-off given the infra cost. Every mechanism above is grounded in the game's own
official docs or, where flagged, the specific Docker image's own documented env vars — not guessed —
but "confirmed via documentation" is not the same claim as "verified running." Recommend a real
smoke test (subscribe → install → confirm the config actually took effect on a next restart) on at
least one representative server per confidence tier before leaning on this for a support-facing
promise.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
# land before that switch happens, not after.

# land before that switch happens, not after.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. .next needs to be writable by it
# (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable. .env is the one
# exception: systemd's EnvironmentFile= reads it as root (PID 1, pre-privilege
# drop) so the app's process env is fine either way, but Prisma's generated
# client ALSO opens .env directly at Client instantiation to resolve its own
# env() directives — that read happens as the actual 'nxeon' process user, so
# a root-owned .env throws EACCES there on every cold start (harmless once
# systemd's injected vars are already in process.env, but noisy, and a prior
# root-run edit to this file silently reverted the ownership fix below once
# already — confirmed live 2026-09-02). Keep .env nxeon-owned, not world- or
# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next/.env ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production web"
systemctl restart nxeon-web

# Drain in-flight provisions before bouncing the worker. Restarting the worker
# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
if [ -n "$DBURL" ] && command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 24); do
    ACTIVE=$(psql "$DBURL" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM \"Job\" WHERE status='RUNNING' AND type='PROVISION';" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break
    echo "==> Waiting for ${ACTIVE} in-flight provision(s) to finish before restarting worker…"
    sleep 10
  done
fi

echo "==> Restarting production worker"
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "PRODUCTION UNHEALTHY — check journalctl -u nxeon-web"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Production promote complete"
